sections.bio: I help AI, SaaS, and technology companies turn complex products into engaging LinkedIn content that builds trust and drives qualified interest. My content focuses on business growth, community building, digital innovation, and practical AI adoption. I create educational, authentic, and insight-driven posts designed to generate meaningful conversations, clicks, and long-term brand awareness. I only collaborate with products that align with my audience and values.

posts.text:
A five minute conversation I'll never forget. 

It wasn't planned.

It wasn't in a boardroom.

It wasn't with a CEO.

It happened while I was waiting to leave.

A gentleman walked up to me, looked at me for a few seconds, and asked,

"Young man, what exactly do you do?"

Without thinking, I replied,

"I'm interested in Business Analysis, Community Management, and Digital Innovation."

He smiled.

Then he asked another question.

One I'll probably remember for the rest of my career.

"That's what you're interested in... but what problem do you solve?"

Silence.

For a few seconds...

I had no answer.

I realised I'd spent so much time learning skills that I'd forgotten the one thing clients actually pay for.

Not titles.

Not certificates.

Not buzzwords.

Solutions.

That five minute conversation completely changed the way I introduce myself.

Now, instead of talking about what I do...

I focus on the problem I want to solve.

I want to help businesses make smarter decisions through data.

I want to help brands build communities people actually care about.

I want to help organisations embrace innovation without losing sight of the people they serve.

Because at the end of the day...

Nobody hires you because you're "passionate."

Nobody hires you because you're "hardworking."

They hire you because you make something easier.

Faster.

Better.

That conversation lasted only five minutes.

But it changed the questions I ask myself every single day.

Now whenever I meet someone new...

I don't ask,

"What do you do?"

I ask,

"What problem are you becoming known for solving?"

Maybe that's the better question.

I'm curious...

If someone introduced you without mentioning your job title...

What problem would they say you're known for solving?

Five minutes. One question. A different way of thinking.

I'd genuinely love to read your answer.


#ARAQGLOBALINNOVATION #BusinessAnalysis #CommunityManagement #DigitalInnovation #Leadership #ProblemSolving #CareerGrowth #PersonalBrand

"I almost deleted my LinkedIn account." 

Some months ago, I opened LinkedIn, looked at my latest post...

12 impressions.

One reaction.

Zero comments.

I laughed.

Not because it was funny.

Because I'd spent almost two hours writing that post.

For a moment, I convinced myself of something dangerous:

"Maybe I'm just not interesting enough."

So I stopped posting.

For weeks.

One evening, I came across a quote that said:

"Nobody starts with an audience. They build one conversation at a time."

That hit me.

The next day, I posted again.

Not because I expected it to go viral.

But because I refused to let one disappointing post decide what I was capable of.

Fast forward to today...

I've met incredible professionals.

Learned from people I never thought I'd connect with.

Reached my first 1,000 followers.

And more importantly...

I stopped measuring my progress by one post.

Now I measure it by one question:

"Did I become better than the person who posted yesterday?"

If you're creating, building, or learning...

Keep going.

Sometimes the breakthrough comes long after you feel like giving up.

If this resonates with you, tell me:

What's one moment that almost made you quit but didn't?

#LinkedIn #CareerGrowth #PersonalBranding #ProfessionalDevelopment #GrowthMindset #Leadership #Community

A few months ago, I was posting... and almost nobody noticed.
I'd spend time writing.
I'd overthink every sentence.
I'd hit "Post."
Then I'd refresh LinkedIn every few minutes hoping something would happen.
Usually...
Nothing.
No big reactions.
No viral reach.
Just silence.
Today, 1,000 people have chosen to follow my journey.
I'm grateful.
But the biggest win isn't the number.
It's what the journey taught me.

10 lessons my first 1,000 followers unknowingly taught me:

1. Nobody owes you attention.
You have to earn it every single post.
2. People don't follow information.
They follow perspective.
3. A great hook is more important than a perfect paragraph.
If nobody reads the first line, the rest doesn't matter.
4. Community is built one conversation at a time.
Comments matter more than likes.
5. Consistency beats motivation.
Some posts performed well.
Some completely flopped.
I kept showing up anyway.
6. Data tells you what happened.
People tell you why it happened.
That's why I believe Business Analysis and Community Management belong together.
7. AI is a tool, not a replacement for original thinking.
Technology can accelerate ideas.
It can't replace genuine curiosity.
8. The best opportunities often come from private messages, not public metrics.
9. 9. Every post teaches you something.
Especially the ones that fail.
10. This is only the beginning.
I'm committed to sharing more about:
📊 Business Growth
👥 Community Building
🤖 AI & Digital Innovation
🚀 Startup Strategy
If you've been following my journey, thank you.
Your comments, ideas, and conversations have shaped it more than you know.
Now I'm curious...
What's the biggest lesson LinkedIn has taught you?
Let's learn from each other.
#LinkedIn #BusinessGrowth #BusinessAnalysis #CommunityManagement #ArtificialIntelligence #DigitalInnovation #Leadership #Startups #PersonalBranding

Yesterday, I watched something that completely changed how I think about business growth.

A founder asked his team a simple question:

Why aren't more people using our product?

The room went silent.

One person said,

We need more marketing.

Another replied,

We should spend more on ads.

Then someone quietly asked,

Have we actually spoken to the users who stopped using it?

Silence again.

That moment stuck with me.

Sometimes we rush to buy more traffic...

...when the real answer is already sitting in our customer feedback.

The businesses that keep improving don't always have the biggest budgets.

They ask better questions.

That's why I'm becoming more convinced that Business Analysis, Community Management, and AI aren't separate disciplines.

Together, they help businesses answer one critical question:

What are our customers trying to tell us?

Before spending more on marketing...

Spend more time listening.

You might discover your next growth opportunity is already in your inbox.

BusinessGrowth
#BusinessAnalysis
#CommunityManagement
#ARAQGLOBALINNOVATION

Every week, I see founders post:

"We reached 100,000 users."

"We hit 1 million visits."

"Our waitlist doubled."

Congratulations.

But here's the question nobody asks:

How many of those users came back this week?

Because growth without retention is just expensive marketing.

A product doesn't become valuable when people try it.

It becomes valuable when people feel the need to return.

That's the metric investors quietly watch.

Take any successful SaaS company.

They don't obsess over downloads.

They obsess over habits.

The companies that win aren't the ones with the biggest launch.

They're the ones that become part of a customer's workflow.

That's why community has become a strategic asset, not a marketing function.

A strong community increases retention.

Retention improves lifetime value.

Higher lifetime value gives you more room to acquire customers profitably.

It's a flywheel not a vanity metric.

Here's the challenge I'd give every founder today: 

If your marketing stopped for 30 days...

Would your existing users still invite others to your product?

If the answer is no...

You don't have a growth engine yet.

You have a traffic engine.

And those are two very different businesses.

Abdulqowiyy Abdulraheem
